newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end year mixed in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end year mixed in sluggish trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed mixed in the final session of the year amid sluggish markets, buoyed only by deals in brewing giant Bavaria and machine-tool and equipment manufacturer Distral SA.
Bogota's IBB index was up 0.15 percent to 844.13 on Friday's close amid a 718 million peso volume. For the year, Bogota ended 11.46 percent up on the 1996 opening price of 757.31.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index drifted down 0.2 percent to 13,423.69, amid a 5.2 billion peso volume. For the year, the Medellin index ended 3.12 percent lower than the 1996 opening price.
"The main feature of the day was the cross-deals in Bavaria and Distral," one Bogota broker said.

Distral said Monday it had agreed to sell an 18 percent stake in the company to German industrial group Deutsche Babcock. More than 3.6 billion pesos in Distral shares were traded in a pocket-to-pocket deal on the Medellin exchange at an unchanged price of 40 pesos each.
About half the session volume in Bogota was made up of a cross-deal in Bavaria at an unchanged 4,100 pesos per share.
The main mover on the Bogota exchange was Banco Ganadero ordinary shares, up 1.18 percent to 256.
The biggest gainer in Medellin was recreational park Villa del Rosario, up 1.82 percent to 7,000 pesos.

"We can sum up the stock markets in 1996 saying that they were boosted by significant investments in major Colombian companies by new strategic partners but overall, grave structural problems persist such as the high concentration of shares in individual shareholders' hands," a Medellin broker said.
"I don't think the situation will change much in 1997. There's no decision on the horizon to order companies to put more shares on to the market," he added.
